title: seller-proofpoint-economics-tacticals-sketch
content:
Purpose: quick seller-facing micro-deck + pocket battlecard focused on converting platform and infra engineers by proving economics with visual proofpoints. This is a rough sketch: not for customer distribution yet.

Audience: SEs, field sellers, platform-engineer-focused AEs. Primary goal: shorten technical qualification -> proof of unit economics (cost/per-token, latency per-transaction) -> pilot sign-off.

Sections / slide notes (high level):

1) Title slide (1 line): "Seller Proofpoints: Economics & Tactical Converts"
   - One-liner: show before/after unit cost with Redwood + 2 fallback paths.
   - Notes to self: need quick visual (bar chart) comparing existing infra, cloud-hosted LLM endpoint, Redwood routing w/ cache.

2) The simple economics frame (2 slides)
   - Slide A: "Total cost per 1k requests" (bullets: token mix assumptions, avg prompt+response tokens, embedding calls)
   - Slide B: "Latency vs cost tradeoff" (mini-heatmap; call out Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private)
   - Seller script snippet: "If they care about p99 latency and deterministic spend, lead with Dedicated commit models; if they need quick dev velocity but unpredictable burst, highlight Hosted with cost caps."

3) Proofpoint visuals (2 slides)
   - Micro-case: ecommerce search rerank (10M monthly queries) — show cost delta and latency tail improvement with prefix caching and batching.
   - Micro-case: customer support summarization (infrequent long sequences) — show caching doesn't help; show fallback to quantized model profile to control cost.

4) Ready-to-run pilot bundle (1 slide)
   - Pilot SKU (3-week): onboard, sample traffic, SLO baseline, 1 optimization pass (batching/caching).
   - What we measure: token cost pre/post, median latency, p95/p99, failure rate, qualitative accuracy sample-set.

5) Seller battlecards / objection handlers (one-pager)
   - Objection: "We already run an LLM on our GPUs." -> Response: "True — baseline ops costs often miss tail and dev time. Show operational delta: observability, rollouts, fallback routing, and dev-time to integrate."
   - Objection: "Quantization causes quality loss." -> Response: "We run model-specific quality checks and recommend staged rollouts with eval prompts; show sample regression threshold and rollback flow."
   - Objection: "We need on-prem for compliance." -> Response: "Private deployment proofpoint: same API, customer controls KMS, audit logs + SLA add-on."

6) Tactical playbook (checklist + quick steps)
   - Quick discovery checklist: (a) avg request size, (b) percent of repeated prefixes, (c) latency SLOs, (d) security constraints.
   - Rapid demo script (30–90s): show hosted API call, toggle cache on, show cost reduction estimate, show fallback to smaller model.

7) Appendix: metrics and formulas (notes to SE)
   - Key formulas: cost_per_1k = (avg_tokens_per_req * token_price) * requests/1000 + infra_margin; latency_effect ~ base_latency * (1 - cache_hit_rate * cache_savings)
   - Example numbers: avg_tokens 350, token_price_hosted $0.0008/1k tokens, dedicated amortized $0.00035/1k tokens (illustrative).

Unresolved / TODOs:
 - Need updated Redwood hosted token pricing table from pricing team (ticket: JIRA-GT-789).
 - Add 2 customer anonymized numbers (ecom & fintech) from CS; ask Priya to scope.
 - Create simple SVG micro-charts for slide 2 and slide 3 (ask design).

Usage notes for sellers:
 - Keep slide deck under 6 slides for discovery calls. Use one-pager battlecard during quick follow-ups.
 - For platform engineers: bring in an SRE/architect quick checklist (networking, headroom, deployment policy).
 - For CFO/Procurement: include committed capacity ROI calc in appendix.

Rough scripts / soundbites (short):
 - "We help you make LLM inference predictable: lower unit cost, preserve latency, and reduce ops surprises — and show the numbers in minutes."
 - "Pilot is low-lift: 3 weeks, measurable econ delta, and a guard-railed rollout path."

Notes to self: keep language non-salesy for technical buyers. Call out tradeoffs transparently. Include clear next step: schedule 45 min pilot kickoff or hand off to solutions engineering.
